flawed_step: Step 1: By total probability, P(S|T)=P(S|T,C)P(C|T)+P(S|T,not-C)P(not-C|T), with an analogous expression for not-T. This is justified. Step 2 would infer the ordering of the two overall weighted averages from the within-stratum inequalities. This is unjustified because the stratum weights P(C|T) and P(C|not-T) can differ.
counterexample: Take a uniform probability space of 10 individuals. The (T,C) cell has 1 individual, successful; the (not-T,C) cell has 4 individuals, 3 successful; the (T,not-C) cell has 4 individuals, 1 successful; and the (not-T,not-C) cell has 1 individual, unsuccessful. Thus P(S|T,C)=1>3/4=P(S|not-T,C), and P(S|T,not-C)=1/4>0=P(S|not-T,not-C). All four cells have positive probability. However, T has 2 successes among 5 individuals, while not-T has 3 successes among 5, so P(S|T)=2/5<3/5=P(S|not-T).
assessment_summary: The statement fails because treatment and alternative groups may have different distributions across strata. Strict superiority within each stratum does not order weighted averages formed with different weights; the explicit 10-person construction gives a strict overall reversal.
